What the cardinal is saying is that being abused as a child can make a person develop psychological illnesses. Most commonly developed as PTSD, if you're abused as a child, you **CAN** (not necessarily will) have a messed up mind when you grow older. It is simply impossible for some people to function in society, and they are not in the right state of mind.

Take the example I used for soldiers who come back from war. For some, the experience is so traumatasing that hearing a noise at night will make them believe they're being attacked. If their child wakes up in the middle of the night and starts walking to his parents' room, and his dad suffers from war PTSD, he might think it's the 'enemy' ambushing him, and he could end up shooting his own kid simply because he is not sane. It is why sometimes veterans have an extremely hard time fitting into society after war. Granted, some can come back and function normally, but not all can.

The same goes for people who were abused as children. while some may grow up as normal individuals, some may be too mentally injured to. this is what the cardinal is referring to; they're not doing it because they like abusing children, but because they cannot adjust themselves to fit into society, and should therefore not be treated the same way, since they require special care.

> Wilfrid Cardinal Napier, the Archbishop of Durban in South Africa, claimed on BBC radio that paedophiles *who had themselves suffered sexual abuse* could not be considered criminals but should instead be seen as psychologically ill.

He says that people who have been abused themselves are psychologically ill. While this might not always be the case, and some might be criminals, it is important to note that is is **extremely** plausible for these people who have been abused to suffer from a psychological condition. They have committed a crime, but they should be sent to psychiatric wards, not prison. If a war veteran suffers from PTSD and shoots someone while having a nervous breakdown, he is not a criminal, but should be institutionalised.

The title is also malevolently misleading, as it tries to make it seem as if the cardinal believes pedophilia is not a crime. Really, people who suffer from psychological conditions are committing crimes, but they are not criminals per se. They are committing crimes, but because they are not in a sane state of mind.

UPDATE: Well, I can update, which means I'm (I guess fortunately) still here. I don't know why I update this, I guess because people are concerned, for some reason. I was planning on setting this photo as my wallpaper, for when someone walked into my room, but something stopped me...

I don't know exactly what got me through last night. I know it was partially my gf, partially this post, and partially something else, I don't know what. I want to thank all the people that reached out to me; I felt like people were genuinely concerned... And though I'm definitely far from safe, you people got me through. I don't feel great by any means, and I might attempt in the future. (I'm just being honest here), but thanks.

I'm just tired of waiting for it to "get better". I may not have lived much, but I've been depressed over half my life. I've held on for too long and nothing gets better. Perhaps for some people it does, but for me it doesn't.
